valuation.net_debt_note: EV = market cap + latest borrowings. Screener's public page does not split cash out of other assets, so cash is not netted off; investments are shown separately.

dcf.method: 5-year FCFF: EBITDA - tax on EBIT - capex - change in net working capital; growth fades linearly from the starting rate to the year-5 rate; Gordon terminal value; equity = EV - borrowings.

inputs.growth_basis: median of 3-year, 5-year and TTM sales growth, capped 0-30%
inputs.capex_rule: depreciation + new sales / fixed-asset turnover (median of the last three years)

reverse_dcf.note: Constant sales growth for five years, at the base margin and the same WACC and terminal growth, that makes the DCF equal today's EV.

blocks.text: Sharvaya Metals is a small aluminium processor: it melts and alloys aluminium (predominantly scrap) and sells the output as alloyed ingots, billets, slabs, sheets and circles, and has more recently added EV battery housings / enclosures [F] (SCREENER). Stated end markets are cookware, automotive, LED lighting, electric vehicles, construction, aerospace and defence [F] (SCREENER). The company was incorporated in 2014 and converted from a private to a public limited company in February 2024 [F] (RATING).

The economics are those of a conversion business. Material was about 93% of cost of sales in FY24, with aluminium scrap the main cost component [F] (RATING), so the company earns a thin spread between metal bought and metal sold. EBITDA margin was 4.6-5.0% in FY22-FY24, 17.0% in FY25 and 8.0% in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS). FY26 revenue was Rs 230 cr, EBITDA Rs 18 cr and PAT Rs 12 cr [F] (NUMBERS).

Customer profile: CARE reports that products are sold to authorised raw-material suppliers of utensil brands such as Hawkins, Prestige and Nirlep, and also to the automobile industry and other industries [MC] (RATING). The brands are therefore indirect, end-of-chain customers, not disclosed direct buyers [AI]. **The end-market % split, the product split, the domestic/export split and customer concentration are not disclosed in any document available to us** [F] (SCREENER; RATING). The company is described as an exporter [F] (SCREENER), but the export share is not disclosed.

subsections.title: Listing status and what it means for the evidence base

blocks.text: Our dashboard's earlier notes record an SME IPO in 2025 and a subsequent move to the mainboard [AI] (BOARD); neither the IPO date, issue size, objects of the issue nor any migration is evidenced in the company documents available to us. Our shareholding data begins in September 2025 with 378 shareholders, rising to 472 by March 2026 [F] (NUMBERS), consistent with a listing around mid-2025 [AI]. Financial results in our statements data are half-yearly (Sep and Mar periods) [F] (NUMBERS), which is the SME reporting pattern; no June 2026 quarter is present, which we cannot reconcile with the mainboard claim [AI].

Evidence base is unusually thin. We had no prospectus, no annual report (the FY26 annual report was filed on 2 Sep 2026 [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS) but was not available to us), no earnings-call transcripts and no investor presentations. The only company-specific third-party document is a CARE rating release dated 25 Oct 2024, which itself was issued under 'Issuer Not Cooperating' status [F] (RATING). Most qualitative sections of this report therefore record non-disclosure as the finding.

blocks.text: Driver classification [AI]: #1 company-specific and partly cyclical (aluminium price level lifts reported revenue); #2 company-specific (one-off equity raise); #3 cyclical (metal-spread driven); #4 company-specific; #5 structural theme but unproven at company level; #6 valuation, not a driver; #7 structural theme with no company evidence.

items: 1. **Margin collapsed in the latest half-year.** EBITDA margin fell to 2.9% in H2 FY26 on Rs 140 cr sales (EBITDA Rs 4 cr, PAT Rs 2 cr) from 16% in H1 FY26 [F] (NUMBERS). No explanation is available to us. Annualised H2 PAT is far below the Rs 12 cr used in the 11.7x P/E [AI].
2. **Profits have not turned into cash.** FY26 CFO was -Rs 34 cr against PAT of Rs 12 cr; 5-year cumulative CFO/PAT is -0.89x and 5-year cumulative FCF -Rs 33 cr [F] (NUMBERS).

3. **The FY25-H1 FY26 margin spike coincides with the pre-IPO window.** Margin was 4.6-5.0% for FY22-FY24 [F] (NUMBERS) in what CARE describes as a highly competitive, fragmented industry with price competition [F] (RATING); it then ran at 16-18% for three consecutive half-years before falling to 2.9% after listing [F] (NUMBERS). The pattern warrants scepticism about the sustainability of the reported peak [AI].

4. **Commodity exposure with thin value-add.** Material ~93% of cost of sales in FY24, aluminium scrap prices volatile [F] (RATING). A +5% un-passed-through input shock on FY26 costs would remove roughly half of FY26 EBITDA [E] (NUMBERS; RATING).

5. **Credit-market conduct.** Bank facilities were rated CARE B / B- under 'Issuer Not Cooperating' from at least Apr 2021 until the company requested withdrawal in Oct 2024 [F] (RATING). A company that did not share information with its rating agency for over three years now asks equity investors for trust [AI].

6. **Working capital is absorbing the growth.** Working-capital days rose from 23 (FY24) to 54 (FY25) to 102 (FY26) [F] (NUMBERS); other assets rose Rs 36 cr to Rs 85 cr in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS), and a residual of roughly Rs 25-30 cr is not explained by inventory and receivables days [E] (NUMBERS).

7. **The DCF does not support the price.** Base-case DCF value Rs 58.4 per share and bear -Rs 39.8 vs price Rs 140; only the bull case (Rs 161.6) is above the price; the reverse DCF implies 77.1% annual sales growth for five years [F] (NUMBERS).

8. **Nothing is disclosed about customers, orders or capacity.** No order book, no customer concentration, no capacity or utilisation figures are available to us [F] (SCREENER; RATING; ANNOUNCEMENTS).

9. **Thin, shifting shareholder base.** 472 shareholders at Mar 2026; FII holding fell from 6.93% to 1.86% within six months [F] (NUMBERS). Price is 33% below the 52-week high of Rs 209 [F] (NUMBERS).

10. **Unreconciled data.** FY24 PAT is Rs 1.00 cr per CARE's audited figures vs Rs 2 cr in our statements data; FY23 EBITDA margin 5.44% vs 4.9% [F] (RATING; NUMBERS). Differences are small in rupees but material relative to the base.

**Is H2 FY26 a one-off or the new normal?** Bull: three prior half-years at 16-18% show capability [F] (NUMBERS). Bear: 4.6-5.0% for FY22-FY24 is the longer record [F] (NUMBERS), and the 2.9% print may simply be reversion [AI]. The FY26 annual report and H1 FY27 results are the evidence that settles this.

**Is 11.7x trailing P/E cheap?** Bull: low multiple for a company that tripled revenue in two years [F] (NUMBERS). Bear: trailing EPS includes H1 FY26 at 16% margin; with CFO negative, earnings are not yet cash [AI].

**Is the working-capital build growth investment or a quality problem?** Doubling revenue needs inventory [AI]; but working-capital days roughly doubled while revenue doubled, meaning capital intensity per rupee of sales rose rather than stayed flat [E] (NUMBERS).
**Is EV housing a business or a label?** It appears in the product list [F] (SCREENER) and in CARE's description [MC] (RATING), but no revenue, customer or qualification milestone is disclosed [F].
**Did the IPO cash fund growth or plug a hole?** FY26 CFF +Rs 38 cr broadly offset CFO -Rs 34 cr and CFI -Rs 3 cr [F] (NUMBERS): the equity raised was consumed by operations within the year [AI].

blocks.text: The market appears to price Sharvaya on trailing earnings (11.7x P/E [F] (NUMBERS)) as a growth micro-cap with EV optionality. Our read is that the trailing earnings are the wrong anchor: the latest half-year earned 2.9% EBITDA margin, cash flow was deeply negative, and the only evidenced customer base is branded-cookware supply chains in a fragmented, price-competitive industry [F] (NUMBERS; RATING) [AI]. The variant view is therefore that this is a commodity remelter whose FY25 margin was the anomaly and whose FY26 margin was already flattered by H1, rather than a specialty-alloy franchise. The view would be wrong if H1 FY27 restores mid-teens margins with positive operating cash flow; that is testable within two months of this report [AI].

blocks.text: Our statements data are standalone [F] (NUMBERS) and CARE's analytical approach was standalone [F] (RATING). Whether consolidated accounts exist cannot be determined from the documents available to us.

The current business is recent in its scale: FY24 revenue of Rs 71 cr was essentially flat on FY23 [F] (NUMBERS), and about 62% of the entire FY22-FY26 revenue increase occurred in FY26 alone [E] (NUMBERS). The corporate actions cluster in a 24-month window: public-company conversion (Feb 2024), rating withdrawal (Oct 2024), capital increases in FY24, FY25 and FY26, and listing in 2025 [F] (RATING; NUMBERS) [AI] (BOARD). **The margin step-up to 16-18% occurs exactly across the pre-listing periods, and reverses in the first full half-year after listing** [F] (NUMBERS). A listed history of two half-years is too short to judge through-cycle economics [AI].

items: 1. Procurement of aluminium scrap (the major material cost component) and, per our earlier notes, primary aluminium for blending [F] (RATING) [AI] (BOARD).
2. Melting and alloying to customer chemistry: 'alloyed ingots' are a listed product [F] (SCREENER); alloy specifications and trace-element control are claimed in our earlier notes only [AI] (BOARD).
3. Casting into ingots, billets and slabs [F] (SCREENER; RATING).
4. Rolling of slabs into sheets and blanking into circles 'of different measurements and sizes as per the requirement of clients' [F] (RATING).
5. Downstream fabrication of EV battery housings / precision EV components [F] (SCREENER) [MC] (RATING).
6. Sale to authorised raw-material suppliers of utensil brands, automobile customers and others [MC] (RATING).

blocks.text: Which of these stages are performed in-house, and at which plant, is not disclosed in the documents available to us [F]. The chain above is inferred from the product list [AI].

blocks.text: Value is captured as a conversion spread over metal cost. With material at about 93% of cost of sales in FY24 [F] (RATING), the spread available to cover labour, power, overheads and profit was single-digit percent, and FY22-FY24 EBITDA margins of 4.6-5.0% [F] (NUMBERS) are consistent with that [AI]. The FY25 margin of 17.0% [F] (NUMBERS) would require either a much richer product mix, a large favourable metal-price or inventory gain, or a change in cost structure; none is disclosed [AI]. CARE states the company passes raw-material increases to clients [MC] (RATING); the H2 FY26 margin of 2.9% [F] (NUMBERS) suggests the pass-through is at best lagged [AI].

Fixed capital is light: net fixed assets were Rs 13 cr at Mar 2026 against Rs 230 cr revenue, a fixed-asset turnover of 17.69x [F] (NUMBERS). Reported depreciation rounds to zero in every year [F] (NUMBERS), which is unusual for a melting and rolling operation and cannot be explained without the notes to accounts [AI]. Working capital is heavy: working-capital days were 102 in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS). The business is fixed-asset-light but working-capital-heavy [AI]. Outsourcing (job work) arrangements are not disclosed.

blocks.text: Ingots, billets and slabs are commodity-like: priced off metal plus a conversion premium, sold in a fragmented market [F] (RATING) [AI]. Circles and sheets sold into branded-cookware supply chains carry some specification and approval element [AI]. EV housings are the only line with a plausible differentiation case, but no revenue, customer or approval is disclosed [F] (SCREENER). On available evidence the portfolio should be treated as commodity-dominated [AI].

subsections.title: What is known for the current year

blocks.text: Nothing about FY27 is known from our documents. The latest period in our statements data is H2 FY26 (half-year to Mar 2026) [F] (NUMBERS). No quarterly or half-yearly FY27 result, deferred order, order inflow or guidance is available. If the company reports half-yearly, the H1 FY27 result (to Sep 2026) is the next data point [AI].

The company is described as manufacturing, supplying and exporting aluminium products [F] (SCREENER), but no export revenue, destination or share is disclosed. CARE mentions competition 'domestically and globally' but gives no export figure [F] (RATING). Whether export mix is changing, and whether by strategy or mix, cannot be assessed.

subsections.title: Currency, trade policy and location risk

items: Currency exposure: not disclosed; hedging policy not disclosed [F]. Aluminium inputs are internationally priced, so rupee moves likely affect input cost even for domestic sales [AI].
Tariffs and trade policy: not assessable because export destinations are undisclosed; no document available to us discusses tariffs [F].
Manufacturing location: plant location(s) are not disclosed in the documents available to us [F]. If operations are single-site, as the scale suggests [AI], a site disruption would halt all revenue.

blocks.text: Concentration cannot be shown either way. The prospectus of a 2025 SME IPO would normally include top-customer data [AI], but it was not available to us. Debtor days of 6-17 in FY24-FY26 [F] (NUMBERS) suggest customers pay quickly or in advance, which is typical of intermediated metal trade [AI].

Source for the names: CARE, reporting that 'SML's products are sold to authorised raw material suppliers of well-known utensil brands such as Hawkins, Prestige and Nirlep' [MC] (RATING). These are not direct customer relationships and no brand-level approval is disclosed [AI]. No case studies are disclosed.

subsections.title: Contracts and the direction of concentration

blocks.text: No long-term agreements are disclosed; the only description of the commercial relationship is 'continuous and repeated orders' [MC] (RATING), i.e. purchase-order business [AI]. Whether concentration is improving or worsening is unknown. The doubling of revenue in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS) could reflect either broader customer acquisition or larger volumes to a few intermediaries; the rise in debtor days from 6 (FY24) to 17 (FY26) [F] (NUMBERS) is consistent with the company extending more credit to win volume, but does not prove it [AI].

This is the only line with third-party evidence of an actual customer channel: products sold to authorised RM suppliers of Hawkins, Prestige and Nirlep [MC] (RATING). The company sits one step upstream of the brand's own raw-material vendors, i.e. two steps from the brand [AI]. What exists today: an evidenced product and channel; what is narrative: any claim of brand approval or preferred status. Government exposure: none evidenced. Strategic implication: volumes tied to cookware demand, pricing tied to metal, and the intermediary layer captures part of the relationship value [AI].

EV battery housings/enclosures are listed as a product [F] (SCREENER) and CARE refers to 'high precision Aluminium components required in Electric Vehicles' [MC] (RATING). No revenue, customer, programme, qualification status, capacity or capex for this line is disclosed. Our earlier notes describe a strategy of supplying custom alloys to EV OEMs localising sourcing [AI] (BOARD), which is an analyst framing, not company disclosure. First CWIP in three years (Rs 2 cr at Mar 2026) [F] (NUMBERS) could relate to new lines but its purpose is not disclosed [AI].

Aerospace and defence appear only as named end markets [F] (SCREENER). No defence approval, government customer, order or revenue is disclosed; government exposure cannot be quantified and on available evidence should be taken as nil [AI].

blocks.text: No installed capacity, production volume or utilisation figure is disclosed in any document available to us. An aggregate utilisation trend therefore cannot be built, and management's explanation for any change is not available.

Fixed-asset turnover rose from 5.86x (FY22) to 9.42x (FY25) and 17.69x (FY26) [F] (NUMBERS). A near-doubling of sales per rupee of fixed assets in one year implies either much higher utilisation of the same plant, higher metal prices lifting revenue per tonne, outsourced/traded volume, or a combination [AI]. We cannot distinguish these; traded volume would carry lower margins and would be consistent with the H2 FY26 margin of 2.9% [F] (NUMBERS) [AI].

subsections.title: Revenue sensitivity to utilisation (not a base case)

blocks.text: Sensitivity only [E]: at FY26 revenue of Rs 230 cr and 8.0% EBITDA margin (NUMBERS), every 10% increment in volume at constant realisation would add about Rs 23 cr of revenue and about Rs 1.8 cr of EBITDA. Because the utilisation starting point is unknown, we cannot say whether any headroom exists. Lease expiries: not disclosed.

Source: our statements data (NUMBERS); capex/EBITDA is our calculation. Capex figures are rounded to whole crores, so FY22-FY24 zeros mean below Rs 0.5 cr, not necessarily nil [AI]. The Rs 2 cr of CWIP at Mar 2026 is the first in the five-year record [F] (NUMBERS), about 15% of net block [E] (NUMBERS; BOARD).

FY24 to FY26 revenue rose by Rs 159 cr [E] (NUMBERS). Over the same two years, capex was about Rs 8 cr [F] (NUMBERS), while working capital per our statements data rose from about Rs 4 cr (23 days on Rs 71 cr) to about Rs 64 cr (102 days on Rs 230 cr) [E] (NUMBERS). **Incremental capital was therefore roughly 90% working capital and 10% fixed assets** [E]; incremental revenue per rupee of incremental capital was about 2.3x [E] (Rs 159 cr over roughly Rs 68 cr). Growth is not being bought with plant; it is being bought with inventory and receivables [AI].

No planned capex, capacity expansion or funding plan is disclosed in the documents available to us; the IPO objects were not available. The DCF model assumes capex equal to depreciation plus new sales divided by a 9.42x fixed-asset turnover [F] (NUMBERS). Classification [AI]: asset-light in fixed capital, capital-heavy in working capital.

Material constituted about 93% of total cost of sales in FY24, with aluminium scrap the major cost component; prices are volatile [F] (RATING). Our earlier notes add primary aluminium for blending [AI] (BOARD). Import dependence by year and country is not disclosed. No price-trend data for aluminium or scrap is contained in the documents available to us, so we do not comment on recent metal-price moves.

Pass-through: CARE states that 'SML pass on the increase in prices of raw material to the clients' [MC] (RATING). The evidence is mixed: CARE itself attributes the FY24 margin decline to increased cost of materials consumed [F] (RATING), and margins have ranged from 2.9% to 18% across half-years [F] (NUMBERS). Pass-through, if it exists, is incomplete or lagged [AI].

subsections.title: What can and cannot be built

blocks.text: No tonnage, capacity, realisation per tonne or conversion cost per tonne is disclosed, so per-unit economics cannot be built. The best available substitute is economics per Rs 100 of revenue [E] (NUMBERS).

Method: line items from our statements data divided by revenue; figures are rounded inputs, so ratios are approximate [E] (NUMBERS). FY26 required about Rs 28 of working capital per Rs 100 of sales to earn Rs 5 of PAT [E].

subsections.title: What would have to be true for unit economics to improve

items: A shift in mix toward specified products (EV housings, brand-approved circles) earning a higher conversion premium per tonne [AI].
Reliable metal-cost pass-through with shorter lags [AI].
Working-capital days returning toward the FY23-FY24 level of 23-27 [F] (NUMBERS) so that growth stops consuming cash [AI].
Disclosure of volumes, so that price and volume effects can be separated [AI].

blocks.text: Our statements data are screener.in standalone figures rounded to whole crores [F] (NUMBERS). At this company's size, rounding moves ratios materially (e.g. FY22 PAT of 'Rs 0 cr'). Results are half-yearly. We had no annual report, notes to accounts or auditor's report, so no line item can be verified against source filings.

Other income nil in every year [F] (NUMBERS): profits are not flattered by treasury income, but idle IPO cash, if any, is earning nothing visible [AI].

Depreciation shows as nil in every year despite Rs 7-13 cr of fixed assets [F] (NUMBERS); either sub-Rs 0.5 cr (rounding) or an accounting treatment worth checking [AI]. The DCF assumes D&A of 3% of sales [F] (NUMBERS), far above reported history.

blocks.text: Without a sourced TAM no share arithmetic is possible, and we decline to create one. Even if a TAM were available, the company's FY26 revenue of Rs 230 cr [F] (NUMBERS) is dominated by metal pass-through value; share of a value-based market would overstate its economic footprint [AI].

Revenue = tonnes sold x (metal price + conversion premium) [AI]. Tonnes are bounded by plant capacity (undisclosed) and working-capital funding (FY26: about 102 days [F] (NUMBERS)); the metal price is external; only the conversion premium reflects company skill [AI]. Industry concentration is low: fragmented, with organised and unorganised players [F] (RATING). blocks.text: All figures [F] (NUMBERS). The bear value is negative because FCFF stays negative in every projected year (-Rs 5.5 cr to -Rs 1.9 cr) and the terminal value is negative [F] (NUMBERS): at a 4% margin the business never funds its own working capital [AI].

Qualitatively [AI]: the bear case's 4% margin matches FY22-FY24 (4.6-5.0%) and sits above H2 FY26 (2.9%) [F] (NUMBERS), so it is not a stress case but a return to history. The bull case needs a 10% margin sustained for five years, which the company has achieved only in FY25 and H1 FY26. We therefore weight the base and bear cases more heavily than the bull, without assigning numerical probabilities.

blocks.text: No disclosed peer set is available, so no peer multiple comparison is made. The earnings base for all multiples is FY26, which contains H1 FY26 at 16% margin and H2 FY26 at 2.9% [F] (NUMBERS); multiples on an H2 run-rate would be much higher [AI].

The DCF values equity at Rs 58.4 per share in the base case, below book value of Rs 77.1 [F] (NUMBERS). This is not an error but a statement that at an 8% margin and 59.7 working-capital days, growth destroys value at a 14.5% WACC: capital absorbed by growth earns less than its cost [AI]. The main model sensitivities are (a) the 3% D&A assumption, much higher than the nil reported depreciation [F] (NUMBERS), which lowers tax on EBIT but also raises modelled capex; and (b) working-capital days, where the model is kinder than FY26 actuals [F] (NUMBERS).

At the base margin, WACC and terminal growth, today's EV requires constant sales growth of 77.1% a year for five years, against a base-case 5-year CAGR equivalent of 19.8% [F] (NUMBERS). History: 3-year sales CAGR 48.7% [F] (NUMBERS); FY22-FY26 CAGR about 53.9% [E] (NUMBERS); FY26 growth about 104% [E] (NUMBERS). The implied rate is above the bull case's starting growth of 43.5% [F] (NUMBERS).

**The price is consistent with the bull case, not the base case**: Rs 140 sits between the base (Rs 58.4) and bull (Rs 161.6) values [F] (NUMBERS), and the reverse DCF asks for 77.1% annual growth at an 8% margin. It is effectively paying for FY25-type margins to return, while the latest half-year printed 2.9% and operating cash flow was -Rs 34 cr [F] (NUMBERS) [AI].

The DCF is mechanically harsh on a working-capital-heavy business in hyper-growth: it charges every rupee of inventory build as lost cash, while the market may reasonably view inventory of aluminium as near-liquid [AI]. If working capital normalises toward the FY23-FY24 level of 23-27 days [F] (NUMBERS) and margins recover even partly, the same model would give a much higher value; the bull case already shows Rs 161.6 at a 10% margin [F] (NUMBERS). A 1.82x P/B for a company with 24% FY26 ROE [F] (NUMBERS) is not stretched on its face.

A company that tripled revenue in two years to Rs 230 cr [F] (NUMBERS), has deleveraged to 0.16x debt/equity [F] (NUMBERS), trades at 11.7x trailing earnings and 1.82x book [F] (NUMBERS), and has shown for three consecutive half-years that it can earn 16-18% EBITDA margins [F] (NUMBERS). A commodity remelter in a fragmented, price-competitive market [F] (RATING), whose peak margins were achieved in the pre-listing window and collapsed to 2.9% in the first full post-listing half-year [F] (NUMBERS), whose profits have not converted to cash (5-year CFO -Rs 25 cr vs PAT Rs 28 cr [E] (NUMBERS)), which did not cooperate with its rating agency for three years [F] (RATING), and whose price sits 2.4x the base-case DCF value [E] (NUMBERS).

items: Downside: the P/E looks low only because FY26 includes a high-margin H1; the H2 run-rate is the fresher datapoint [AI].

blocks.text: Source: our DCF model [F] (NUMBERS). The payoff is asymmetric to the downside on the model's own terms [AI].

The model's range runs from FY31 sales of Rs 345 cr at a 4% margin (bear) to Rs 784 cr at a 10% margin (bull) [F] (NUMBERS). The spread is driven far more by margin than by growth; the investment question is therefore which margin regime is real, and the data needed to answer it (volumes, product mix, pass-through terms) are not disclosed [AI].

At Rs 140 the shares trade well above the base-case DCF value of Rs 58.4 and the bear value of -Rs 39.8, and modestly below the bull value of Rs 161.6 [F] (NUMBERS). The gap to the base case is explained by the market capitalising FY26 earnings that included a 16%-margin first half, while the model uses an 8% margin and charges for the heavy working-capital build [AI]. The reverse DCF (77.1% implied growth) makes the same point [F] (NUMBERS).

The evidence base is too thin to underwrite the bull case: no annual report, transcripts, capacity, customer or segment data were available to us. For investors with a horizon beyond two years, the relevant question is whether the company can show a through-cycle margin and positive cash flow; neither is yet evidenced [AI].

summary.one_line: Sharvaya Metals has tripled revenue to Rs 230 cr in two years, but its margin collapsed to 2.9% in H2 FY26, profits have not converted to cash, disclosure is minimal, and at Rs 140 the price sits well above the base-case DCF value of Rs 58.4 and close to the bull value of Rs 161.6.
